overview: This file brings together U.S. and British reporting on Japanese efforts to secure strategic base-metal ores immediately before and during the Pacific War. A May 1941 telegram reports rapidly increasing bauxite shipments from the Netherlands East Indies to Japan; a group of 1940 memoranda and letters documents Mitsubishi's attempt to buy Argentine tungsten concentrates at above-market prices; and a March 1942 London despatch encloses a detailed British Ministry of Economic Warfare assessment of Japan's bauxite stocks, aluminum capacity, and newly controlled sources in the Netherlands East Indies, Malaya, and the Caroline Islands. The latter includes production and export statistics, ore-quality data, mine locations, transport facilities, and estimates of prospective wartime output.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Grew on bauxite exports to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports the growth of bauxite exports from the Netherlands East Indies to Japan and the larger quota fixed for 1941.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Japan's bauxite imports from the Netherlands Indies rising sharply, with an even bigger 1941 quota set.

subfiles.title: Memorandum requesting acknowledgment of Chandler letter
subfiles.about: Requests preparation of an acknowledgment to Charles Lyon Chandler's attached confidential letter.
subfiles.summary: Memo routes correspondence on Japanese tungsten purchases in Argentina for an acknowledgment to be drafted.

subfiles.title: Chandler letter on Japanese tungsten purchasing in Argentina
subfiles.about: Transmits confidential information concerning Mitsubishi efforts to secure long-term supplies of Argentine tungsten concentrates.
subfiles.summary: Chandler reports Mitsubishi aggressively bidding above US prices for Argentine tungsten, already buying through intermediaries.

subfiles.title: Duggan acknowledgment to Chandler
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Chandler's confidential report on Japanese attempts to purchase tungsten concentrates.
subfiles.summary: Duggan thanks Chandler for reporting on Japanese tungsten purchasing in Argentina.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Buenos Aires enclosing Chandler's letter
subfiles.to: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Forwards Chandler's letter to the U.S. mission in Buenos Aires for confidential information.
subfiles.summary: State forwards Chandler's confidential letter on Japanese tungsten buying in Argentina to the embassy there.

subfiles.title: London despatch transmitting assessment of Japanese bauxite resources
subfiles.from: James Somerville, for the Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, U.S. Embassy London
subfiles.about: Transmits a British Ministry of Economic Warfare memorandum and charts assessing Japan's bauxite resources and supply prospects.
subfiles.summary: London despatch estimates Japan's 1942 bauxite stockpile could sustain two years of aluminum output, with Indies and Malayan mines able to expand further.

subfiles.title: Ministry of Economic Warfare memorandum on Japanese bauxite resources
subfiles.to: Enclosed with U.S. Embassy London Despatch No. 3282
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japanese bauxite stocks, consumption, supply sources, mines, ore quality, transport facilities, and production potential.
subfiles.summary: British economic-warfare memo details Japan's bauxite imports, stockpiles, and potential output from captured Indies, Malayan, and Caroline Islands mines.

interest: Shows Japan outbidding the US for tungsten in Argentina, and Allied estimates of Japan's wartime bauxite and aluminum capacity.
